request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Oura by TxPipe maintenance over 12 months, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve, with a total withdrawal of 540,750 ADA including a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee.
Oura is described as a Rust-native pipeline tool that connects to Cardano nodes, monitors blockchain events, and routes matching patterns to pluggable outputs.
Oura supports multiple data sources including N2C, N2N, S3, Mithril, and UTxO RPC, and supports sinks including Kafka, Elasticsearch, AWS services, RabbitMQ, Redis, SQL databases, and webhooks.
The document says Oura has 654 commits, 288 stars, 79 forks, and 58 contributors, and identifies the GitHub repository where these figures can be checked.
The proposer states Oura is used across the ecosystem for indexing, monitoring, analytics, and real-time event processing.
The proposer states Oura has been funded twice through Project Catalyst, in Funds 9 and 13, for feature development.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting and audit materials.
The proposer states the requested withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.
The document states independent oversight will be provided by Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
The document states TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 successfully delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

summary: The anchor describes a 540,750 ADA treasury withdrawal administered by Intersect for 12 months of Oura maintenance, community support, documentation, and AI-workflow compatibility work, with claims of existing adoption, prior funding history, Intersect budget-process support, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based oversight.
